title: Pilot: harder targets, stage 1, 4 setups × 2 runs, $0.20 a lab (Nov 9), left out

design.question: For the same agents and checker, how much money does each way of organizing the labs spend to reach the same number of targets?
design.compare: OSO, α 0.2, Shared library, Planner, Pay per lemma
design.fixed: the same 4 agents (the single agent: the first, with all the money), $0.80 in all, Lean checks every proof
design.measure: median money, all labs together, to reach 5 of the 11 targets; 5 is the highest count that more than half the runs of every setup reached; a run that never got there counts as not reached

answer: Median money, all labs together, to reach 5 of the 11 targets: OSO, α 0.2 $0.316; Shared library $0.593; Planner $0.223; Pay per lemma $0.607. OSO, α 0.2 minus Shared library: −$0.276. OSO, α 0.2 minus Planner: +$0.093. OSO, α 0.2 minus Pay per lemma: −$0.291.

table.settings: shared at once · α 1 · lab 1 assigns the work
shared at once · each new result pays its author · α 1

caveats: Labs could not stop early: each worked until its money or the rounds ran out, so setups are compared at the same money spent.

Rewards differ from the current simulation model: the knowledge reward is off (the simulation pays 1 per new bit since v5): Lean has no agreed measure of a result's new knowledge yet, see docs/design.md; value flowing back is split by the lines each parent saves (its own proof's length in symbols), a stand-in for the work it saves (1/p) in the simulation.

Money to a count is all labs together, to the end of the round that reached it. Medians have ranges of at least 95% from the sorted runs; differences of medians have 95% ranges from resampling the runs; runs are not paired. Other table values are mean ± standard deviation.
In the planner setup lab 1 only plans, so three labs prove and most of its money stays unspent; it is also told to save the team money and how to split the work.
